text:
Situation: As of 2026-10-21, bumetanide injection has been on the FDA shortage list for 106 months since the initial posting on 2017-12-13. FDA records show shortage entries for Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc., Sagent Pharmaceuticals, Fresenius Kabi USA LLC, MSN Laboratories Private Limited, and Mullan Pharmaceutical Inc. all reflect resolved status with an update date of 2026-09-30. Corvale East holds 85 units of the 10 mL multidose vial (5.7 days) and 21 units of the 4 mL single-dose vial (1.4 days). Corvale General has approximately 19 days of total bumetanide supply at current usage rates. Tablet inventory at both sites exceeds 30 days.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the bumetanide injection shortage on 2017-12-13. As of 2026-10-21, the shortage has been listed for 106 months. All five manufacturer shortage entries show resolved status updated 2026-09-30. Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. (FEI 2220525) is a registered plant for bumetanide 0.25 mg/mL with manufacture, analysis, and labeling operations. FDA inspections of Hikma's plant from 2009 through 2024 were classified VAI, most recently ending 2024-06-12 with a known date of 2024-12-16. The plant's last inspection was NAI on 2026-05-13.

Our position: The FDA shortage list still reflects an active posting for bumetanide injection despite all manufacturer entries showing resolved status as of 2026-09-30. Hikma's plant has an acceptable inspection history with a recent NAI classification. P&T has already approved Hikma's bumetanide 0.25 mg/mL (NDC 00641600710) as a same-product alternate manufacturer option on 2026-07-01. Sagent's product received similar approval on 2026-08-25. Current injection supply at Corvale East is critically low.

Recommended actions:
1. Procure Hikma bumetanide 0.25 mg/mL 10 mL multidose vials to replenish Corvale East stock — requires buyer approval.
2. Procure Hikma bumetanide 0.25 mg/mL 4 mL single-dose vials to replenish Corvale East stock — requires buyer approval.
3. Activate Sagent Pharmaceuticals bumetanide 0.25 mg/mL as secondary source if Hikma allocation is limited — requires pharmacist verification and buyer approval.
4. Monitor FDA shortage list for status change from active to resolved — requires buyer to track weekly.

Not recommended: Purchasing from A-S Medication Solutions, Advagen Pharma Limited, or American Health Packaging because their labels do not identify a manufacturing plant we can verify and they are not on the FDA shortage list.
